verdicts.why: The Brotherhood stage starts at X-Men (2000), which this record doesn't cover. In The Wolverine's post-credits scene he only comes with Xavier to warn Logan, which doesn't plainly make him a member, so the X-Men stage stays at Days of Future Past (unsure, so the existing stage is kept).

MCU Wiki 'Leaving PRIDE' (RW110): Catherine and Geoffrey decide to have nothing more to do with Jonah or PRIDE and skip the next meeting. 'Return to PRIDE' (RW201): they rejoin to search for the Runaways.

Weapon X/Team X and Alpha Flight both come before the X-Men in his history and are shown only in flashback or dialogue (he 'eventually left' Alpha Flight, and in S2E5 he refuses to rejoin). Neither membership is held in the series' present. The '97 S2 Team X and X-Men stages stay.

Confirmed: after losing her powers in '97 S1 E3, 'a shell-shocked Storm decided to leave the team', and she returns at Xavier's call by E9 (Gold Team). The stage title must use the record's season form, 'X-Men '97 S1', not 'X-Men '97'.

Marvel Database: after Jean's sacrifice the remorseful Phoenix revived her, 'which then left'. Jean returned to the X-Men without it (its Host is now listed only as 'Formerly: Jean Grey'), and its '97 return is brief. So the entity's last stage should not be the X-Men.

Supported: he 'inserted himself onto the team' (the Resistance), then has Peter 'clock him out forever' at Drive Max, and B-15 sends the Resistance members home. Not supported: the TVA ending, which comes only from a wiki line citing promo or extra material. Wikipedia's plot has no TVA job, so it is too unsure to use, and he ends Independent.
At Wade's request B-15 returns the Resistance members to their respective homes, so the team breaks up. Laura stays with Logan in Wade's universe, and the infobox lists the Resistance as 'formerly'.
Before the series 'she left the Brotherhood' and was contacted by Xavier. Her Brotherhood past is backstory, shown only in flashback (A Rogue's Tale), and she is already an X-Man in TAS.

Before the series 'he left her and the guild'. In S2E6 he helps the Thieves but tells Bella Donna he is 'neither a thief nor an assassin, but an X-Man' and leaves, so there is no Thieves Guild membership during the series.

At the end of TAS he leaves with Lilandra and wills leadership of the X-Men to Magneto. In '97 he is presented to the Shi'ar as her consort, then in S1E8 'he left the Shi'ar behind to return to Earth'. 'Shi'ar Empire' is a group name the dataset already uses.

The Nasty Boys stage breaks the rules: Morph served Sinister only while 'brainwashed', which is mind control, not a move. The rest holds up: once free he was 'not ready to rejoin' and fled (S2E2), rejoined and left again in S4E3 (ep 51), and 'after the Professor's departure... rejoined the team on a permanent basis' ('97 S1E1).

Correct that he becomes 'a full-fledged member of the X-Men' only in '97 S1E1. In TAS he only teams up with them. But 'The Resistance' is the dataset's name for the Void team in Deadpool & Wolverine, and the source only says 'the mutant resistance', not a plain group name. So the 2055 stage is dropped rather than merged into that group; the owner can add it under a separate name.
Marvel Database lists 'Formerly: X-Men'. In '97 S1E9 he is put on a team with the X-Men against Bastion, and in E10 he is listed as AWOL on Forge's X-Men roster. He then forms X-Force.

The TAS retirement holds: after Cortez's betrayal and losing Asteroid M he 'retired to the Arctic Circle' (S5E2), then leads Genosha. The OZT stage breaks the rules: he was 'kidnapped and imprisoned by Bastion', and being held is not a move. The final Independent is unsure (in E9 he acts alone, which is not a move, and in E10 and Egypt he is with the X-Men, current affiliation X-Men), so the existing Genosha last stage is kept.

'Kurt eventually joined Genosha's council as outreach for any communities of faith' ('97 S1E5), and 'Following the attack, Kurt joined the X-Men as an official team member' (S1E7). 'Genosha' is a group name the dataset already uses.
Under 'Joining the X-Men' ('97 S1E9), Forge and Storm rejoin the X-Men at Xavier's call and he is put on the Gold Team, so the X-Men stage starts in S1, not S2.
'Archangel later moved to Genosha and was present at the Gala' ('97 S1E5). Cable then recruits him into X-Force. The dataset already uses Genosha for its residents (Banshee, Moira, Callisto).

In Blade II, Blade 'was placed in command of the Bloodpack', and the sewer battle 'marked the end of the Bloodpack as a group'. The infobox lists Bloodpack and Nightstalkers as former affiliations, and 'The Bloodpack' is a group name the dataset already uses.

In S2 (RW208-212) she says PRIDE can disband and moves to shut the Church down. The adepts depose and imprison her, and after the rescue she shelters with the Runaways. In S3 (RW306) she returns to the Church and 'decided to build it back up'.
In RW304 Xavin, disguised as Victor Stein, takes Elle onto the Magistrates' ship and leaves Earth 'with Elle as her new mother', and never comes back. That is a departure from the Runaways in S3.
St. Theresa's Church is a workplace (a parish he takes over), and neither the record nor the dataset tracks it as a group. Under the owner's rule, workplaces the record doesn't track are rejected.
In Endgame he stays in the past with Peggy and retires ('Enjoying his long retirement'), handing the shield to Sam. The infobox lists the Avengers as 'formerly'.
This twin's first title is The Winter Soldier, where he is already HYDRA's asset. His 107th/U.S. Army and Howling Commandos service is WWII backstory that ended with his fall from the train.
'By 2012, Carter had retired from S.H.I.E.L.D. and was living in the United Kingdom'. She is still at S.H.I.E.L.D. in the 1989 Ant-Man scene and retired by The Winter Soldier.
